newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end sharply higher in modest trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end sharply higher in modest trade.

text.p: The Manila share index, propelled by gains in selected B shares and blue chips, jumped 1.08 percent, closing at 2,705.92 points on Wednesday, traders said.
"The market's rebounding from its lows but it is still tentative. We still don't think highly of it," said Fitz Aclan, research head at Dharmala Securities Phils Inc.
Turnover was modest at two billion pesos against the average daily volume of 2.7 to 2.9 billion.
"The B shares such as those of Meralco rose basically on news that the Securities and Exchange Commission will not force declassification of shares," said Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities.
Meralco B, one of the most heavily traded issues, ended 15 percent higher at 129 pesos.
Traders said movement in speculative and thirdliner issues such as Forum Pacific Inc and Abacus Consolidated Resources Inc B were noticeable during late trade.
"Since the market is moving sideways overall, investors are resuming interest in small cap issues," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
Despite the uptick in the main index, there were almost the same number of gainers at 66 and losers 65 with 66 issues unchanged.
HSBC James Capel Securities Phils Inc research head Minda Olonan said that market is in a consolidation phase and that any rally may be taken as a cue to further reduce exposure.
Summit's Liu, however, said that a reversal may be in place if the index pierces through the 2,710 resistance point.
